title: You Don't Beat The Beast — You Survive Her
flavorText: When she steps through the ropes there is no music, no smile, no games. Just destruction. The WOW World Champion plowed through her own roster like a wrecking ball — overpowering, outlasting, outright obliterating anyone who dared stand across from her. Her powerbomb doesn't just end matches. It ends hope. Tonight you are not asked to beat The Beast. You are asked to do what almost nobody has: survive her… if you're lucky.
objective: Survive a match against The Beast without being defeated.
setupInstructions: Set up a standard Last Man Standing match against The Beast. She doesn't talk much — she doesn't need to — so the silence rule is in force: neither wrestler may play taunt cards this match. Pick any wrestler to face her; the challenge is measured in survival, not gold.
conditions: The Beast is your opponent; you may play any wrestler.
Survival is the only victory — being pinned, submitting, or failing the 10-count is defeat. Outlast her.
modifiers: Silence: she doesn't talk, and neither can you — neither wrestler may play taunt cards this match.
It ends hope: the first time The Beast lands her powerbomb, you lose 1 extra [[health]] — there are no wasted motions, only pain.
notes: Slot 1 of Season 2. Teaches that challenges can ask for different things — here, survival instead of victory.

title: Belt Collector — King of the Indies
flavorText: Many wrestlers have laid claim to the moniker of greatest of all time, but only one can crown himself the undisputed king of the indies. Matt Cardona left the world's largest wrestling promotion in 2020 and instantly conquered the indie scene, winning titles wherever he went — at any given moment holding no less than 8 championships at the same time. Now the Deathmatch King has set his eyes on a kingdom of a different kind. The road to a throne of his own starts with one more crown.
objective: Win a match as Matt Cardona.
setupInstructions: Standard setup. Play as Matt Cardona. Every win is an investment — every championship is leverage — so start the collection: this is part one of the Belt Collector arc.
conditions: The belt collector is always working: win the match while keeping at least 1 [[momentum]] unspent — a champion never goes all-in on the first deal.
notes: Slot 2 of Season 2 and part one of three of the Belt Collector arc (ATW-byhj). Part two goes hardcore, part three goes gauntlet.

title: Raven — What About Me?
flavorText: A former World Champion and a hardcore legend, Raven is a great brawler and a vicious individual — but his greatest strength is the combination of unrivalled genius and charisma. A master manipulator, he uses psychological warfare to guarantee victory before the match even starts, and the flock of followers he cultivated in every promotion would do anything to protect him. He asks the question that gnaws at him: what about me? What about Raven? Answer him in the ring — if the flock lets you.
objective: Defeat Raven despite the Flock's interference saves.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match against Raven. Quote the Raven, nevermore — but expect the flock to have the final word at least twice.
conditions: Raven is your opponent in a No DQ match — weapons are legal and psychological warfare is already underway.
The flock answers their master: twice per match, the moment Raven is about to lose, a Flock member interferes to save him. You must put him away a third time to win.
modifiers: Psychological warfare: Raven starts the match with 2 [[momentum]] — his games began before the bell.
Even flow: whenever Raven lands a successful strike, he gains +1 extra [[momentum]] — the flock feeds on his dominance.
notes: Slot 3 of Season 2 and the first modifier wall: plan around the two interference saves or stall out.

title: Brian Pillman — Loose Cannon
flavorText: An All-American NFL Bengal turned two-time light heavyweight champion, Brian Pillman became something else entirely in the mid-1990s: increasingly erratic, uncontrollable, unpredictable, and capable of anything. His words and actions shocked fans and wrestlers alike — one of the hottest wrestlers of the decade, a member of the Four Horsemen. Now awoken to a second chance, Pillman is on the loose, looking to upheave, looking for trouble, and nobody can even predict what he is going to do next.
objective: Defeat Brian Pillman under randomly rolled modifiers.
setupInstructions: Set up a No DQ match against Pillman. Before the match, roll 2d6 and apply the two random modifiers whose numbers you rolled — nobody, including the game, can predict what the Loose Cannon brings tonight.
conditions: Random-modifier roll: before the match, roll 2d6 and apply BOTH rolled modifiers from the list below. Reroll duplicates.

Roll table — 1: Pillman starts with +2 [[momentum]]; 2: weapons deal +1 [[health]] all match; 3: Pillman may make one free attack after each of your pins attempt fails; 4: your recover actions heal 1 less [[stamina]]; 5: Pillman's first pin attempt each turn is automatic; 6: both wrestlers deal +1 [[health]] on successful strikes.
notes: Slot 4 of Season 2 and the variance debut — the random roll teaches adaptability before streak content ever requires it.

title: Sgt. Slaughter — The Hero
flavorText: Before the betrayal and the boos, there was the hero. Sgt. Slaughter rose to iconic status as one of the most feared villains in the ring — the Cobra Clutch few ever escaped — and then defended his country against The Iron Shaikh, becoming arguably the most popular wrestler in the world. Immortalized in G.I. Joe comics and toy lines to this very day, he is at his peak: a fan favorite, an American hero, a drill sergeant who never lost his grip. Tonight, the crowd is behind him — give them the hero's walk they remember.
objective: Win by submission with the Cobra Clutch as the crowd rallies behind you.
setupInstructions: Set up a Submission match playing as Sgt. Slaughter. Win the way the hero always did — make your opponent tap to the Cobra Clutch. Listen up, maggot: the crowd expects nothing less. And that is an Orrrrderrr!
conditions: Play as Sgt. Slaughter; the only acceptable victory is a submission finish.
Crowd-heat flavor: you start with the crowd fully behind you — narrate each of your comebacks like a hero's rally as the match goes on.
notes: Slot 5 of Season 2 and act 1 of the Slaughter rise-fall-redemption arc (ATW-xl1k): the hero the crowd loves, before act 2 turns them.
